Your first quest by hand:
This walks through writing a small side quest by hand, starting from an empty file. The quest is offered in the bar at Thunder Station in Sol and asks you to fly to Sirius. For every field and rule, see [[Modding]]. The fan-made [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/mods/ Quest Editor] writes the same file for you and checks it, which is the easier route. == 1. Make the file == Create a text file named Quest150.json. Any number from 0 to 199 works; the game tells quests apart by the ''ID'' inside, not the file name. Use a plain text editor, since a word processor swaps straight quotes for curly ones and the game cannot read those. == 2. Paste in the quest == 
{
  "settings": {
    "QuestName": "A Quiet Delivery",
    "QuestDescription": "I need someone to fly out to Sirius. No questions.",
    "ID": 9100,
    "Lang": "en",
    "StationName": "Thunder Station",
    "CharName": "Mira",
    "CharImage": "Tourist1",
    "MinKarma": -101,
    "MaxKarma": 101,
    "Faction": "none",
    "FactionMinRep": 0,
    "isRandomSpaceQuest": false,
    "RequestedQuestIDCompleted": ""
  },
  "BarRumors": [],
  "questParts": [
    {
      "name": "Briefing",
      "TODO": "Listen to Mira.",
      "questID": 0,
      "isCheckPoint": true,
      "dialogText": [
        {
          "Name": "Mira",
          "showTimeSec": 8,
          "character": "Tourist1",
          "options": "",
          "text": "Fly to Sirius for me. Someone there is expecting you."
        }
      ],
      "repeatTextTimeSec": 999999999,
      "completeAction": "ACTION_DIALOG_COMPLETE"
    },
    {
      "name": "Fly to Sirius",
      "TODO": "Jump to Sirius.",
      "questID": 0,
      "isCheckPoint": true,
      "dialogText": [],
      "repeatTextTimeSec": 999999999,
      "completeAction": "ACTION_WARP_END_SYSTEM_Sirius"
    }
  ]
}
What each part does: * '''settings''' says who offers the quest and where. StationName is the station whose bar offers it, spelled exactly as in the game. Lang must match your game's language: en, ru, es, pt or cn. * '''ID''' must be a number no other loaded quest uses. The game's own quests use 100002 to 100044. * '''MinKarma''' and '''MaxKarma''' of -101 and 101 mean anyone can take it. * '''questParts''' are the steps, in order. A quest needs at least two. The first shows Mira's message and ends when the message is closed. The second ends when you arrive in Sirius, and then the quest is complete. * '''isCheckPoint''' saves the quest on entering the step, so a reload resumes there. == 3. Copy it to the game == Put the file straight into this folder on your phone, not in a folder of its own: 
Android/data/com.skvgames.GalaxyGenome/files/Quest150.json
== 4. Switch it on == Open '''Modifications''' from the main menu. The '''Side Quests''' section shows the folder it reads from and whether a mod file '''exists''' there. If it does, switch Side Quests on and allow the game to access your files when it asks. == 5. Get it offered == Fly to Sol, dock at Thunder Station and open the bar. The bar offers nothing until you '''buy a drink'''. The first drink of a visit offers one quest, picked at random from every quest that bar can give, so at a busy bar it may take a few tries: close the bar, warp out and back, and buy another drink. Your quest is only offered while one of your three quest slots is free. == Common mistakes == * '''The file is in a folder of its own.''' The game only reads files placed directly in the folder above. * '''The JSON is broken.''' A missing comma or a curly quote makes the game skip the whole file without a message. Paste it into a JSON validator to check. * '''Only one step.''' A quest with fewer than two steps is skipped. * '''The ID is taken.''' A second quest with the same ID is skipped. * '''The station name is misspelled''', or Lang does not match your game's language. * '''An action starts with BUTTON_.''' The game adds that itself, so leave it off. * '''The game updated.''' Every mod is switched off after an update; turn them back on. Mods also make [[Combat#Rating battles|Rating battles]] unavailable while they are active.
Your first star system by hand:
This walks through adding a new star system by hand: one star, two planets, and a station orbiting a planet. For every field and rule, see [[Modding#Stars, planets and stations|Modding]]. The fan-made [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/mods/new/stars Quest Editor] builds the same file for you on a map, which is the easier route. == 1. Make the file == Stars, planets and stations all go in one file, which must be named exactly StarsStations.json. Use a plain text editor, since curly quotes break the file. == 2. Paste in the system == 
{
  "Stars": [
    {
      "Name": "Harbor Star",
      "type": "K-YellowOrange",
      "X": 3,
      "Y": -4,
      "Z": 0,
      "security": "Anarchy"
    }
  ],
  "Planets": [
    {
      "Name": "Harbor I",
      "system": "Harbor Star",
      "type": "RockPlanet",
      "dist": 400,
      "sput": 0,
      "size": 2000,
      "rings": 0
    },
    {
      "Name": "Harbor II",
      "system": "Harbor Star",
      "type": "GasGiantClassI",
      "dist": 1500,
      "sput": 2,
      "size": 30000,
      "rings": 1
    }
  ],
  "Stations": [
    {
      "Name": "Harbor Dock",
      "StarSystem": "Harbor Star",
      "PlanetID": 2,
      "type": "NovaStation",
      "Faction": "Independent"
    }
  ]
}
== 3. The star == * '''X''' and '''Y''' place the star on the [[Galaxy Genome Map|galaxy map]], in light years, with Sol at 0, 0. '''Z''' is its height above or below the map. Pick a point no other system uses; 3, -4 is 5 light years from Sol with no system within 2 light years. * '''security''' is one of Anarchy, Low, Medium, High, Only, NoOne or Conflict. Left out or misspelled, it is Anarchy. A station in an Anarchy system has a black market. [[Modding#Security levels|Security levels]] lists the pirates and guards each brings. * '''type''' is a star type from the list on [[Modding]]. Left out or misspelled, it is M-RedDwarf. == 4. The planets == * '''system''' is the star's Name. * '''dist''' is the orbit. Planet orbits are rounded down to a multiple of 100, and a planet at an orbit its system already uses is skipped, so 420 and 480 in the same system leave only the first. * '''sput''' is the number of moons, '''rings''' 1 for rings, and '''size''' the planet's size. == 5. The station == * '''StarSystem''' must be a star listed in the '''Stars''' of this same file. A station whose system is not there is skipped. * '''PlanetID''' is which body it orbits, counting the bodies listed for that system from 1, belts included. For a new star that is the order of the Planets list, so 2 is Harbor II. The body must be a planet or an asteroid belt, not a star. See [[Modding#What PlanetID counts|what PlanetID counts]]. * '''Faction''' uses different names from a quest's settings: Russian (United Empire), USA (Trade Federation), China (Interstellar Alliance), Independent or Pirates. * '''type''' is one of OrbitalDark, OrbitalWhite, NovaStation, FarmStation, StationHighTech or AsteroidStation. A station with any of these fields missing is skipped, and so is one named like a station the game already has. == Adding a station to an existing system == A Stars entry with the name of an existing system '''changes that system''': its position, security and type all become what the entry says, with the defaults above for anything left out. So to put a station in an existing system, list the system in Stars with its exact current X, Y, Z, security and type. A guess moves the system or changes its security. The station's PlanetID then counts any bodies the game already lists for that system first. Sagittarius A* cannot be changed. == 6. Copy it to the game == Put the file straight into this folder on your phone: 
Android/data/com.skvgames.GalaxyGenome/files/StarsStations.json
On Android 11 and later the phone's own file manager cannot open Android/data; the [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/mods/help/installing Quest Editor's install guide] shows ways around it. Then open '''Modifications''' from the main menu, check the '''Stars and Stations''' section says the file '''exists''', switch it on and allow the game to access your files. The new system appears on the galaxy map, and its planets start out discovered. == Common mistakes == * '''The file has another name''', or sits in a folder of its own. * '''The station's system is not in Stars.''' Even for an existing system, the station needs it listed. * '''PlanetID counts from 0''', or points at a star. It counts from 1 and must land on a planet or a belt. * '''Two planets share an orbit''' once rounded down to 100. The second is skipped. * '''An existing system was listed with guessed values''', which moves it or changes its security. * '''The game updated.''' Every mod is switched off after an update; turn them back on.
Modules:
Modules are what your hull actually does. Every one takes a slot, most take
'''mass''', and mass is subtracted from how far you can jump, so outfitting is a
series of trades rather than a shopping list.

== Classes and Grades ==
Every module has a '''class''' and a '''grade''', written together: a '''4D''' is
class 4, grade D.

'''Class''' is the number, from 1 to 9. Every hull has a largest class it will
take in each slot; see [[Ships#What a hull will take|Ships]].

Stations often sell classes 1-3 of some module types, and 1-9 of others. If
you're looking for a specific high-class module, use our map to find a station
that sells the higher class modules, like
[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=DeepSpaceDrive this link for stations that sell all classes of warp drives].

'''Grade''' is the letter, in five steps from '''E''' to '''A'''. A better grade
performs better, but it is not simply "buy A": grade also changes '''mass''',
and not in one direction. Comparing one warp drive class across its grades:

{| class="fandom-table"
! Grade !! Mass
|-
| E || 2.5
|-
| D || 1
|-
| C || 2.5
|-
| B || 3.5
|-
| A || 2.5
|}

'''D is the lightest.''' That is why experienced players fit D almost everywhere
and spend the weight budget on the one module where raw performance wins, the
warp drive.

Two module types do not follow that shape. '''Shields''' lose mass steadily from E to A,
so there the best grade is also the lightest. '''Fuel tanks''' are sold at C grade
only.

=== A bigger class at D beats a smaller class at A ===
Grade is the expensive axis and class is the cheap one, which is worth knowing
before spending a fortune on an A. A '''4D''' Fuel Scoop against a '''3A''':

{| class="fandom-table"
!  !! Scoop speed !! Mass !! Power !! Cost (CR)
|-
| 3A || 0.176 || 0.4 || 0.48 || 901,000
|-
| 4D || 0.196 || 0.4 || 0.33 || 44,000
|}

The 4D scoops faster, draws less power, weighs the same and costs a twentieth as
much. Check the class your hull will take before paying for grade: see
[[Ships#What a hull will take|Ships]].

== Core modules ==
Every hull carries one of each of these, and none of them can be removed, only
replaced with another class or grade.

{| class="fandom-table sortable"
! Module !! What the game says it does
|-
| Hull || ''“The type of spacecraft hull affects the resistance to various types of damage.”''
|-
| Power Plant || ''“Produces energy which is then consumed by all the spacecraft modules.”''
|-
| Power Distributor || ''“Regulates the distribution of power from the Power Plant between the ship's main subsystems”''
|-
| Thrusters || ''“Thrusters are responsible for acceleration and angular rate of spacecraft.”''
|-
| Warp Drive || ''“This engine type is used for travelling between different star systems.”''
|-
| Life Support || ''“Turns on if the spacecraft is critically damaged, and allows you to control the spacecraft for some time even if it is depressurized.”''
|-
| Sensors || ''“Used for detecting the nearest spacecrafts and objects.”''
|}

Hulls come in four types, '''Light''', '''Reinforced''', '''Mirrored''' and
'''Military''', each resisting damage differently.

'''Engineers can modify most of these.''' See [[Module Mods]].

== Cargo racks ==
Eight classes, capacity doubling each time, and '''no mass at any of them''', so
the only cost is credits and a slot. The table, and what a full load is worth,
are in [[Trading#Cargo racks|Trading]].

== Fuel tanks and scooping ==
Tank size sets how far you can travel between stars.

{| class="fandom-table sortable"
! Class !! Fuel !! Cost (CR)
|-
| 1C || 2 || 1,000
|-
| 2C || 4 || 3,800
|-
| 3C || 8 || 7,090
|-
| 4C || 16 || 25,090
|-
| 5C || 32 || 98,970
|-
| 6C || 64 || 345,000
|-
| 7C || 128 || 1,780,930
|}

A '''Fuel Scoop''' refills the tank from a star, and that is what makes deep
space possible at all. Only some [[The galaxy#Star types|star types]] can be scooped, so a
long route is really a route between the ones that can, and an unscoopable star
is a dead end however convenient it looks.

Hold a middle distance while scooping: too close and the ship overheats, too far
and the scoop stops collecting.

== Scanners ==
The '''Planet Scanner''' is what earns you money from exploring, and its range is
the whole point — a longer scanner discovers planets from further out, so you fly
less per system. The '''1D''' costs 1,000 CR, weighs nothing and more than doubles
what the average system pays you for turning up; every grade after it costs
between eleven and three hundred times as much for roughly a tenth of that gain.
See [[Exploration#What each grade is actually worth|Exploration]].

Other scanners do narrower jobs:
* '''Cargo Scanner''' — reads another ship's hold. ''"Turns on automatically when there is a target."''
* '''[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=PirateScanner Criminals Scanner]''' — reads whether a target is wanted, and '''increases the elimination reward'''. See [[Combat]].
* '''Energy wakes scanner''' and '''Spectrum Analyzer''' — specialist survey gear.

== Mining modules ==
'''Mining Laser''', '''Seismic charges''' and the '''Collector Drone Controller'''
are covered in full on [[Mining]], including which ships can see where to aim.

== Weapons and defence ==
Weapon choice is a question of '''thermal''' against '''kinetic''' damage, and
the defensive modules are mostly about managing '''heat'''. Both are covered on
[[Combat]].

== Repair Module ==
''"Allows to repair other modules in case there are enough spare parts."'' It is
the one way to mend modules away from a station. Its panel is in the ship's menu
and lists your '''Damaged Modules'''. ''"When you select the module you want to
repair, it will be disabled and the repair process will start."'' The module
switches back on once it is at full integrity. The power plant is the exception
and keeps running while it is repaired.

Each repair uses '''Repair parts''', and the module holds a limited stock.
''"You can replenish the stock of spare parts by synthesizing them from resources
that you can get in the asteroid belts. Therefore, it is advisable to have a
mining laser installed on your ship."'' '''Make parts''' turns 1 Bouxite and 1
Coltan from your hold into 100 parts, up to the module's capacity. A station
refills it too.

== Damaged modules ==
''"In case of severe damage there can be problems with module functioning so try
to repair modules at stations."'' A module below 20% integrity switches off.
Before that, some fail at random, more often the lower they are:

* '''Thrusters''' below 70% cut out for a moment (''"MODULE ERROR:"'').
* A '''Warp Drive''' below 90% can fail the jump at the end of the countdown.
* '''Life Support''' below 80% loses oxygen faster.
* A weapon below 40% jams now and then, and below 10% on every shot.
* '''Sensors''' work only while the power plant is above 50%.


== Modules you cannot simply buy ==
'''Nothing in an outfitter is gated by faction, reputation or standing.''' Walk
in with the credits and it is yours, which is the opposite of how
[[Ships|ships]] work.

Three modules are different. They appear in no shop at all until you unlock
them, and from that moment '''every''' shop carries them, whatever its purpose.

{| class="fandom-table sortable"
! Module !! Classes !! How it unlocks
|-
| Warp Drive Booster || 3C-5C || Reach '''Arena level 60''', or visit one particular system. See [[Spoilers#The Warp Drive Booster|Spoilers]]
|-
| Gauss Gun || 2D-4D || Complete the side quest ''[[Side quests##10 Dissection|#10 Dissection]]'' (Dr. Landau, [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=93%20Ceti&station=Frontier%20Lab Frontier Lab])
|-

=== Shadow jump module ===
''"A module that replaces the afterburner with Zentarks technology for local
teleportation."''

'''It takes over the boost button.''' With one fitted, pressing boost no longer
lights the afterburner; it teleports you. Which means fitting it costs you boost
entirely, and there is no way to have both.

Where you land depends on whether you have a target selected:

* '''With a target within 700 units''' you arrive '''400 units in front of it''', facing the way it faces.
* '''With no target, or one further than 700 units''', you jump '''800 units ahead''' of your own heading.

The jump takes '''2 seconds''', during which your ship fades out and back in, and
it draws the same power the afterburner would have. That two-second window is the
whole risk: you are committed, visible and not shooting.

It exists in exactly one version, '''3D''', at '''3,200,000 CR''' and 4
mass — heavy for a class 3 module, and there is no lighter grade to fall back on.

=== Experimental Booster ===
''"A module that improves some ship parameters."'' No shop sells one. The first
time you complete each [[Spoilers#Expeditions|expedition]] it pays
'''10,000,000 CR''' and a ''Unique Module'': an Experimental Booster, left in
your module storage at [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=93%20Ceti&station=Frontier%20Lab Frontier Lab].

== Going further ==
Any module can be pushed past its shop grade by an engineer, paid in materials
you collect by landing on planets. See [[Module Mods]].
Galaxy Genome Map:
The '''Galaxy Genome Map''' answers the question every one of these
guides ends on: '''where do I actually go?'''

It draws every catalogued system and generates the rest exactly the way the game
does, so a system you have never visited already knows its planets, its belts and
what percentage of each ore they hold. It runs in a browser, on a phone or a
computer, and nothing needs installing.

The map fills the screen. Along the bottom are '''Filters''' and '''Route''', and
beside them a chip for each filter that is on; tap a chip to take that filter off.
Each one opens a panel from the bottom, which you drag up for more or down to see
more of the map. The search bar at the top finds systems, stations and articles.

Tap a star to select it. The panel shows its name, distance and security, then
what it holds; drag it up for every planet, belt, material and station, with
'''Route here''', '''Read about''' and '''Share'''.

== Route ==
Open '''Route''' and fill in '''From''' and '''To''', by typing a name or tapping
a star: while Route is open, a tapped star fills whichever end is empty. With
From set and To empty, the crosshair in the middle of the map plots the course to
wherever you pan. The panel gives the jumps and light years flown and the longest
single jump on the way, and '''Swap''' and '''Clear''' do what they say.

'''Max jump''' starts at your ship's jump range when you have [[#Other tools|loaded a save]].

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?from=Sol&to=Rakdos&jump=10 Sol to Rakdos at 10 ly] against [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?from=Sol&to=Rakdos&jump=33 the same trip at 33 ly]

Routes run through generated space as well as the catalogue, so the answer is the
real one rather than a catalogue-only guess. They use a [[Navigation#Warp gates|warp
gate]] only once you tick both its ends in the list of repaired gates under Route;
every gate starts broken, so none are ticked until you say so.

== Show me… ==
Whole questions, one tap each, at the top of '''Filters'''. A chip sets the
filters, opens the section that holds its answer and says how many systems
qualify; tap it again to clear it.

* '''High-value scans''': systems that bank 500,000 CR on arrival with a 1D scanner, framed from Sol
* '''Best outfitters''': every Hi-Tech station
* '''Your station's five''': the systems your abandoned [[Your space station|space station]] can be waiting in
* '''Black market run''': stations that sell contraband
* '''Best systems for reputation''', '''Rating battles''', '''Engineers''' and '''Warp gates''', the last two with spoilers on

Below the chips, one section per subject folds open at a time, each with a
'''📖''' that opens its article and a count of what it has set.

== Exploration ==
A [[Exploration|scan]] can be worth 1,500 CR or 1,150,000 CR, and the difference is
invisible until you arrive. Set your '''Planet Scanner''' first, because every
value on the map answers to it: stars pay the moment you drop out of warp, planets
only once they are inside your scanner's range.

* '''Min value''' keeps systems banking at least that much '''on arrival'''. Tick ''Use one-hop value'' to count the one body worth crossing the system for as well.
* '''Planet type present''', '''Min planets''' and '''StarHunter class''' narrow it by what the system holds.

Systems the game already counts as ''explored'' score zero, so nothing on the list
is a wasted trip.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?value=500000&scanner=1D Systems that pay 500,000 CR on arrival with a 1D]
* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?ptype=WaterGiant Systems with a Water Giant], the best single object there is
* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?startype=WolfRayetStar Where the Wolf Rayet Stars are]

Swap the scanner to '''1A''' and the list grows; swap it to ''none fitted'' and it
nearly empties, which is the clearest argument for buying a scanner there is.

== Mining ==
[[Mining|Mining]] pays on percentage, not luck. Pick an ore and the '''Min %'''
slider starts a quarter of the way into that ore's range; raise it to find the rich
belts. A selected system names the belt and its orbit.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?ore=Painite&pct=40 Painite belts at 40% or better]
* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?ore=Alexandrite Anywhere holding Alexandrite]

[[Mining#Deep materials|Void Opal and Musgravite]] are in the list too. They have no
share of a belt, so matching systems are labelled '''3–6 t''' and '''Min %''' is
off.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?ore=VoidOpal Systems with Void Opal]

== Trading ==
A station's market is one kind of thing, so these choices are one at a time:
'''sells contraband''', '''buys contraband''', '''best ore price''', '''buys
trophies''' or '''no market at all'''. Each chip shows how many systems match.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?filters=sellsBlack Every station that is ever dealt the black market]

== Outfitting ==
[[Stations]] stock different things, the game never says which is which, and a
wasted trip is a wasted hour.

Pick a '''Module for sale''' and the map marks every system that stocks it.
'''All classes''' is on by default, so the marks are the shops selling every
class ('''››'''); turn it off to include shops capped lower ('''›'''). A selected
system names the station and gives its model, which is the only handle the game
gives you once you are in the system. '''Shop purpose''' narrows it to stations of
one or more purposes.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=FuelScoop Stations selling a Fuel Scoop]
* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?purpose=HiTech Every Hi-Tech station]

== Faction ==
Pick one or more [[Factions|factions]] to see where their stations are. Faction
combines with Outfitting, so you can ask for a module sold by one faction.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?faction=United%20Empire&filters=station Where United Empire stations are], for the [[Ships|ships]] only they sell

== Security ==
Pick one or more security levels, from High down to Anarchy and Conflict.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?security=A The anarchy systems]

== Module Mods ==
[[Module Mods#Materials|Materials]] come from planet surfaces, and only four planet
types can be landed on. '''Material to dig''' marks the systems with a planet that
yields the one you pick, labelled with the chance a dig turns it up: one figure,
or low to high when several planets there carry it. '''Min %''' works as it does
for ores, and keeps systems where at least one planet reaches it.

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?mat=Phosphorus Systems with a planet that yields Phosphorus]
* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?mat=Germanium&mpct=14 Germanium at its best odds]

* [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?landable=3&lymax=200 Systems with 3 or more landable planets within 200 ly]

== Reputation ==
[[Reputation and ranks|Reputation]] comes fastest from stations close to their
star. Set how close, and the section lists the best systems for each faction,
nearest first: from the system in your save when one is loaded, otherwise from
Sol. Tap a row to select that system.

== Rating battles ==
The '''Rating battles''' section lists all 83 levels of the

== Jump to and Legend ==
* '''Jump to''' flies to Sol, The Void, Sagittarius A*, Isar, Terminus or the whole galaxy. Where a place has a warp gate, the '''⇄''' button flies to the gate's other end.
* The four rarest stars (Preon, Quark, Wolf Rayet and Soft Gamma Repeater Magnetar) are drawn as '''gold diamonds at every zoom'''.

== Other tools ==
The map is one tab of the same app as this wiki.

* '''Loadouts''' has the calculators: pick a ship and its modules, add cargo and fuel, and it gives the jump range, speed, turn rate and shield strength in the game's own units. See [[Navigation]] for why a heavy load shortens a jump.
* '''Save''' loads your game's save. The map then knows your current system and your ship's jump range. The spoiler and language settings are there too.
* '''Wiki''' holds every article, and an article opens over the map without leaving it. A map link in an article moves the map to what it names.
* '''Share''' gives a link that opens on exactly what you are looking at: every filter, the selected system and the view.

== Things worth knowing ==
* '''Spoilers are off by default.''' Engineers, warp gates and The Void stay hidden until you turn spoilers on.
* It '''speaks five languages''', using the game's own words for ores, planets and ships.
* It is '''not''' made by SKV Games. Without a save it knows what the game generates, not what you have done.
The galaxy:
Only a small part of the galaxy is hand-built. The rest is '''generated''': the
game fills space from a density map, and every system's stars, planets and belts
come from a seed derived from its position. That is why a system you have never
visited already has fixed contents, and why they are the same for every player.

* '''14,906''' systems are catalogued, with real star names. Of those, '''5,340''' lie in the region reachable from Sol.
* Everything beyond them is generated on demand and named after its sector and cell, like ''Actox Bw-Ar D68''.

Generated systems are ordinary in every way that matters: they have planets,
belts, ores and scan value, and you can route through them. What they never have
is a [[Stations|station]], an engineer or a mission.

The [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/ Galaxy Genome Map] renders both kinds together.

== Um, what? How did you do that? ==
The counts on this page are not estimates or samples. Every star in the galaxy
was counted.

That is possible because '''the galaxy is not stored anywhere'''. Nobody sat down
and placed 72 million stars, and the game does not ship a list of them. What it
ships is a '''recipe''': a picture of where space is crowded, and a set of rules
for turning any position in that picture into the stars that live there.

When you warp somewhere, the game is not looking the system up. It is working it
out, from scratch, on the spot. Fly away and it forgets; fly back and it works
out the same answer again.

That is why a system you have never visited already has fixed contents, and why
your galaxy and every other player's are identical. There is nothing to
disagree about. Same recipe, same result, every time, for everyone.

=== So it can be run outside the game ===
A recipe can be followed by anyone who has it. The rules were read out of the
game and rewritten so they could be run without playing, and then simply pointed
at every part of the galaxy in turn, writing down what came back.

{| class="fandom-table"
!  !! 
|-
| Places in the galaxy that hold stars || 2,950,361
|-
| Stars worked out and identified || 57,047,273
|-
| Distinct kinds of star found || 58
|}

So when this page says there are 65 Wolf Rayet
Stars, that is not a guess from a sample. Something looked at all
57,056,080 stars, and 65 of them were Wolf
Rayet Stars.

The catalogue's own 8,807 stars are added on top of the
57,047,273 the generator places, because a few kinds exist only there. The
[[Spoilers|Preon star]] is the extreme case: the generator will never make one,
and the galaxy holds exactly one.

One star is not in that count. The '''Preon star''' is never generated anywhere;
there is exactly one in the galaxy and it was placed by hand. It is the single
most valuable thing you can discover, and it is on the [[Spoilers]] page.

=== The part that is easy to get wrong ===
Following the recipe slightly wrong does not produce an error. It produces a
different galaxy, one that looks completely believable and is completely wrong.

So the numbers here were checked against real systems in the real game until they
agreed, rather than trusted because the program ran without complaining.

=== What this cannot tell you ===
It knows what the game '''makes'''. It does not know what '''you''' have done:
what you have already scanned, what a mission will pay you today, or anything
else that lives in your save. Where a number here disagrees with your game, your
game is right.

=== Thank you, SKV Games ===
None of this would be here without '''SKV Games''', who own Galaxy Genome and who
were asked, plainly, whether this could be built and published — and said yes.

They did not have to. A studio is well within its rights to say no to having its
game taken apart and written up by strangers, and plenty would. Instead the
answer was immediate and generous, and the result is a reference far more
detailed than a fan site has any business having.

So if this wiki saves you an evening of guesswork, the credit for that belongs
with the people who made the game and then let us do this with it. Go buy their
game. It is good, and it is the reason any of us are here.

== The Warp Drive Booster ==
The '''[[Spoilers#The Warp Drive Booster|Warp Drive Booster]]''' is the only module that extends jump
range beyond what a drive alone gives you, and no station sells it until you have
done one of two things.

The first is to reach '''Arena level 60''' in [[Combat|ranked battles]].

The second is to '''visit [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Sagittarius%20A%2A Sagittarius A*]''',
the black hole at the centre of the galaxy, 25, 25,899 · 25,899 ly from Sol.
Arriving once is enough; the game records the visit and every outfitter in the
galaxy stocks the Booster from then on.

That is the same trip as the '''Massive and Dangerous'''
[[Achievements|achievement]], so the pilgrimage pays twice.

It is worth seeing what that means. The module that makes long-range travel
possible is locked behind either a combat grind or a journey you need long-range
travel to survive. Going the long way is a genuine expedition: fuel, scooping,
and a route through empty sky, and the reward is that every trip after it is
shorter.

Module Mods:
An engineer can make a module you already own '''stronger than anything a shop
sells''': more damage, faster shield recovery, longer jumps, less mass. The game
calls these '''modifications'''. They cost no credits at all, only
[[#Materials|materials]], and materials are good for nothing else.

The most an engineer can give each part of your ship, before any mass the
modification adds:

* '''Sensor range +75%''' from ''Long Range'' on the [[Modules#Core modules|Sensors]], at level 25
* '''Jump range +55%''' from ''Jump Range'' on the [[Navigation#If you cannot reach somewhere, upgrade the drive|Warp Drive]], at level 25
* '''Shield recovery +50%''' from ''Rapid Charge'' on the [[Combat#Shields, hull and heat|Shields]], at level 25
* '''Damage +36%''' from ''Emitter power'' on the [[Combat#Weapons|Gauss Gun]], at level 15
* '''Rate of fire +30%''' from ''Charging mechanism'' on the [[Combat#Weapons|Missiles]], at level 15
* '''Power capacity +24%''' from ''Power Generation'' on the [[Modules#Core modules|Power Plant]], at level 15
* '''Top speed +18.3%''' from ''Dirty Modification'' on the [[Modules#Core modules|Thrusters]], at level 25
* '''Firing range +18%''' from ''Aimed shooting'' on the [[Combat#Weapons|Beam Laser]], at level 15
* '''Shield strength +15%''' from ''Low Power'' on the [[Combat#Shields, hull and heat|Shields]], at level 25

== How modifications work ==
* '''One modification per module.''' Each module has one to three to choose from. Installing a different one asks ''"Installing a different modification will remove the current modification. Continue with the installation?"'' and starts the new one at level 1.
* '''Levels 1 to 25.''' Each level adds '''a twenty-fifth''' of the modification's full effect, so level 10 is 40% of it and level 25 is all of it.
* '''Engineers cap the level.''' Each engineer is qualified to take a module to level 10, 15 or 25. Past that the game says ''"Engineer's qualification does not allow installing a higher level modification."''
* '''Every level costs materials.''' One of each of two materials, which change every five levels. See [[#What each level costs|what each level costs]].
* '''Effects multiply the module's own figures.''' Shield strength +15% is 15% more of what that shield already gives, so a modification is worth most on the best module you can fit.

Landing needs a '''Planetary Vehicle''' aboard. You take it down,
drive, and dig: each successful dig yields one material. Landing pays no credits
and nothing else in the game counts it, apart from one step of the side quest
[[Side quests##8 Pathfinder|#8 Pathfinder]].

=== Before you land ===
Choose the planet in the system and press '''LANDING'''. It goes down only when:
* a '''Planetary Vehicle''' is fitted, switched on and above 10% integrity, or the game says ''Missing module'', ''No power'' or ''Damaged'';
* the planet is a Rock, Icy, High Metal or Metal Rich planet, or it says ''"PLANET TYPE NOT AVAILABLE FOR LANDING"''.

The vehicle comes in two versions, both class 2, so it needs a class 2 optional
or military slot:

=== On the surface ===
* '''Fuel is the time limit.''' The vehicle lands with a full tank every time. Driving uses it at 2 a second, or 1 in '''low gear''' (a third of the top speed), and the lift thrusters use 1 a second more. A full tank is ten minutes of driving, twenty in low gear. With the tank empty the vehicle stops.
* '''The vehicle's hull is the module's integrity.''' Hard landings and crashes take up to 3% a hit, and the damage stays on the module when you leave. At zero the vehicle stops; repair the module at a station.
* '''To dig''', stop on ground tilted less than about 30° and press the drill. It takes '''2 seconds''' and fails if you move (''"Mining failure: position Change"'') or the ground is too steep (''"Mining failure: uneven surface"''). The scanner shows where material lies; drilling anywhere else gives ''"No resources found"''.
* '''Each deposit gives one material''' and is then used up. You can hold at most '''50''' of each material; past that the game says ''"Material limit reached"'' and the find is lost.
* '''To leave''', hold the take-off button for 3 seconds (''"Return preparation completed"''). You can leave at any time, with or without fuel.

=== Which of a planet's three you get ===
A planet that yields materials carries '''three''', fixed when the system was

planet holding Iron alongside Polonium yields Iron five times as often.
Navigation:
Getting somewhere has two halves that work nothing like each other: '''warp
jumps''' between stars, and '''flying''' once you arrive.

== Jumping between stars ==
Plot a route on the galaxy map and jump one star at a time. The heads-up display
counts down '''JUMPS LEFT''' and names the '''NEXT STAR''', so a long trip is a
sequence of identical short actions.

A jump refuses to happen for five specific reasons, and the game names each:

{| class="fandom-table"
! Message !! What it means
|-
| ''Error: Make a route'' || No destination plotted
|-
| ''Error: Stop the ship'' || You must be stationary to jump
|-
| ''WARP ERROR: TURN OFF CANNONS'' || Weapons must be stowed
|-
| ''Error: Not enough fuel'' || The tank will not cover the jump
|-
| ''No power: warp drive'' || The drive has no power allocated
|}

'''A long route is flown one jump at a time.''' ''"If your warp drive doesn't
allow you to jump in a certain system, you have to repeat the jump after the ship
has stopped."'' You leave the warp still moving, so each next jump waits until
the ship has stopped. A Warp Drive below 90% integrity can also fail the jump at
the end of the countdown; jump again. See [[Modules#Damaged modules|Damaged modules]].

'''Watch the fuel bar.''' ''"Pay attention to the fuel gauges. The white part
shows the amount of fuel needed for a warp jump."'' The white end of the bar is
the next jump's fuel. It disappears when the tank holds less than that jump needs.

'''Where you drop out.''' ''"The process of leaving the warp is always
unpredictable. The spaceship may stop too close to the star which subsequently
leads to overheating."'' You leave the warp on the line you jumped along, heading
in towards the middle of the system. How far out depends on the largest star:
further around a big one, and further again with more than one star or around a
neutron star or black hole. Around an ordinary star that point is already within
its heat, and the ship is still drifting inwards.

== If you cannot reach somewhere, upgrade the drive ==
'''Jump range is the single thing that opens the galaxy up.''' If a system is out
of reach, the answer is almost never a different route, it is a better
'''[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=DeepSpaceDrive Warp Drive]'''.

Range is not a fixed number. It falls as your ship gets heavier, so a full hold
jumps shorter than an empty one, and every module you bolt on costs a little
distance. This is why '''D-grade modules''' are worth fitting nearly everywhere:
they are the lightest, and the weight you save comes back as range. See
[[Modules#Classes and Grades|Modules]].

Two things extend range beyond the drive itself:
* '''[[Spoilers#The Warp Drive Booster|Warp Drive Booster]]''' — ''"used to boost the output of Warp Drive, increasing jump distance."'' '''No shop stocks it until you unlock it''', and then every shop does. See [[Modules#Modules you cannot simply buy|Modules]]
* A bigger '''[[Modules#Fuel tanks and scooping|Fuel Tank]]''' does not add range, but it adds how many jumps you can make before you must find a scoopable star. See [[Modules#Fuel tanks and scooping|fuel]].

The [[Galaxy Genome Map]] plans routes at whatever jump range you give it, so you
can see exactly what a drive upgrade would buy before you pay for it.

== Warp supercharge, and the button you have to press ==
A few things multiply your jump range outright. The ship shop calls it
'''''Build-In Warp Supercharge''''' and prints the multiplier next to it.

{| class="fandom-table"
! Source !! Multiplier !! How you get it
|-
| Prometheus || x3 || Built into the ship
|-
| Nemesis || x5 || Built into the ship
|-
| Neutron star || x5 || Scoop fuel from one, about six seconds
|}

They do not stack. If you are flying a supercharged ship and scooping a neutron
star, you get the '''higher''' of the two, not the product.

=== ROUTE only supercharges the first jump ===
'''This is the part that makes people think their expensive ship is broken.'''
The two route buttons plot differently:

* '''ROUTE''' plots the whole trip for you, but it only applies the multiplier to the '''first jump'''. Every leg after that is planned at your plain jump range, so a supercharged ship routes exactly like an ordinary one.
* '''ADD''' appends one hop to the route, and it applies the multiplier to '''every''' hop.

So the way to actually use a supercharge across a long trip is to centre each
star in turn and press '''ADD''', building the route by hand. It is more taps,
and it is the difference between a Nemesis jumping its range and
jumping five times its range.

=== It is a fuel discount too ===
The multiplier does not only extend the reach. Fuel for a supercharged jump is
charged as though the distance were divided by the multiplier, so a x3 jump
costs the fuel of a jump a third as long. Over a crossing of the galaxy that
matters more than the range does. On a supercharged ship the discount applies
only to jumps longer than your plain range; a shorter jump costs full fuel.
Scooping a neutron star discounts every jump by five.

=== The cost ===
Every jump longer than your unassisted range takes '''1% off your warp drive's
integrity''', supercharged or not. A drive at low integrity jumps shorter, so a
long supercharged run degrades the very thing making it possible. Repair at any
station with an outfitter.

Scooping a neutron star until the drive takes damage is also what unlocks the
'''Risky Refueling''' [[Achievements|achievement]].

For the other two gates, [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?from=Wolf%201462&to=Isar Wolf 1462 ↔ Isar] and [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?from=PPM%2041187&to=Terminus PPM 41187 ↔ Terminus]: repair the Sol end with a Zentarks Stone and 30,000,000 CR, then save and reload.

On the map, tick your repaired ends under '''Gates repaired''' to route through them.

=== Getting a Zentarks Stone ===
* '''Zentarks vs Anglers''', a random deep-space event: an Angler Mother attacks three SARF scouts. Every scout alive when it ends drops a stone.
* '''SARF scouts in the [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Eagle%20Nebula Eagle Nebula]''' drop a stone when destroyed. A Zentarks ship turns up there 40% of the time, half of them scouts.

==== Farming the Zentarks vs Anglers event ====
[[File:Zentarks vs Angler signal.png|thumb|The event on the system map: a Signal Source with a threat level]]
[[File:Zentarks vs Angler objects.png|thumb|The same signal in the list of objects]]
[[File:Zentarks vs Angler ships.png|thumb|The right event: an Angler-Mother and three Zentarks Scouts]]
The event only happens in '''deep space''': a system with no stations, more than
300 ly from Sol and more than 150 ly from the Void. A system gets up to three
events, and each time you arrive, each event's type is drawn again from five
deep-space types. So once you find a system that shows a signal, jumping out and
back re-rolls it.

# Find a deep-space system with a '''Signal Source'''. Players report that ''Rho Bb-Dy E23'', next to [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=93%20Ceti 93 Ceti], works.
# Check the threat level. Zentarks vs Anglers is always '''2, 3 or 4'''. A 0, 1 or 5 is a different event.
# Fly to it. The right event shows an '''Angler-Mother''' and three '''Zentarks Scouts''' in the ship list. Anything else: jump to a neighbour and back.
# '''Kill the Angler-Mother and keep the scouts alive.''' Each scout still alive when the Mother dies drops one stone, so one event gives up to three. Killing a scout yourself gives nothing here.

How many events a system has never changes; only their types do. Rho Bb-Dy E23
has one, so about one arrival in five is the right event. A system with three
gets it on about half of all arrivals.

The map's [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?filters=signals Signal sources] filter, under
Exploration, shows the systems that have events, and a system's card reads
''Signal sources 3 / 3'' for one with three. Two pairs of three-event systems
sit close together, so every arrival is at a system with three:
[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Alcyone Alcyone] ↔ [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Celaeno Celaeno], and
[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Delta%20Tj-%C2%88v%20D5 Delta Tj-v D5] ↔ [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=HIP%2092622 HIP 92622],
12.4 ly apart.

=== Flying through a gate ===
A repaired gate is not a button. You fly into it, and three things must be true
at once, or you pass straight through:

* both ends repaired;
* your speed above '''30%''' of your ship's maximum;
* your heading within '''10 degrees''' of the gate's axis.

Line up on the gate from a distance and hold your course. After a jump the gate
ignores you for five seconds, so you cannot bounce straight back.

== Flying inside a system ==
[[File:Ship menu.png|thumb|The ship menu holds Autopilot, System Map and Warp Jump]]
Once you arrive, distances are measured in '''light seconds''' and your speed in
'''ls/s'''. Planets are further apart than they look.

'''[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=Thrusters Thrusters]''' are ''"responsible for acceleration and angular rate
of spacecraft"'' — how fast you get up to speed and how quickly you turn, not how
fast you end up going.

'''Autopilot''' flies you to whatever you have selected. It is the right way to
cross a system while you do something else, and it is how you approach a station
without overshooting.

== Boost ==
The boost button, the triangle in the flight interface, is an afterburner. It
fails in exactly two situations, and the game tells you which:

* ''"BOOST: not enough energy"'' — your engines do not have the power. Power is divided between engines, systems and weapons, so boost competes with your shields and guns for the same budget.
* ''"BOOST: too high speed"'' — you are already going too fast for it to add anything.

That first one is the one to remember: if boost keeps failing, the fix is the
power distribution, not the engines.
== Geeking out: what mass actually costs you ==
Mass is the price of every module, and it is not charged evenly. Three different
things depend on it, in three different ways.

=== Jump range falls in direct proportion ===
Range is divided by your total mass:

 range ∝ drive's optimal mass ÷ (ship + modules + cargo)

Straight inverse proportion. '''Twice the mass, half the range.''' Nothing else
in the game punishes weight this hard, which is why a warp drive is the one place
to spend grade on performance and everywhere else to spend it on being light.

Note what is inside that bracket: '''cargo counts'''. A full hold really does
jump shorter than an empty one, so the last leg home is always your longest.

=== Speed falls by the square root ===
Top speed uses a square root instead:

 top speed ∝ √(thrusters' optimal mass ÷ (ship + cargo + fuel))

So the same weight that halves your range costs you only '''29%''' of your speed.

{| class="fandom-table"
! Mass !! Jump range !! Top speed !! Acceleration and turn rate
|-
| 1.00x || 100% || 100% || 100%
|-
| 1.25x || 80% || 89% || 89%
|-
| 1.50x || 67% || 82% || 82%
|-
| 2.00x || 50% || 71% || 71%
|-
| 3.00x || 33% || 58% || 58%
|}

=== Handling is just top speed, renamed ===
This is the part worth knowing. '''Acceleration''' and '''turn rate''' are not
separate statistics: the game derives both from top speed.

 acceleration = top speed ÷ 4.5 turn rate    = top speed ÷ 10

So one number governs how fast you go, how fast you get there, and how quickly
you come about. Anything that raises top speed makes the ship handle better in
every respect, and '''[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?module=Thrusters Thrusters]''' are the module that sets it.

=== Putting it together ===
* For '''exploring''', mass is everything. Fit D grades, carry no cargo you do not need, and put the savings into the drive.
* For '''fighting''', mass is cheap. You lose a little speed and handling, and [[Combat#Shields, hull and heat|shields]] are unaffected by what you load.
* For '''hauling''', the cargo is the point, and the cost is range on the loaded leg. Plan the route for the full hold, not the empty one.

Events and Tasks:
Two systems hand you work you did not go looking for. The '''Daily Task''' is one
job a day that everyone in the game shares, and '''star system events''' are
encounters that appear while you fly. Both pay credits, and both are a steady
source of [[Module Mods#Where materials come from|materials]].

== The Daily Task ==
One task per day, shown under '''Daily Task''', with a countdown to the reset.

'''Everyone gets the same task.''' It is generated from the calendar date alone,
with nothing about you in it, so the task you have is the task every other player
has that day. It resets at '''00:00 UTC''', not at midnight where you live.

'''It needs the internet.''' The clock comes from a time server rather than your
device, which is why you will see ''"No internet connection..."'' where the task
should be. You cannot do a Daily Task offline, and you cannot reroll one by
changing your phone's clock.

On top of the credits, finishing the Daily Task pays '''x3 of two random

=== Finding them on the system map ===
''"Yellow exclamation points on the system map indicate random events. According
to the level of danger, you can estimate the risks of flying to this place."''
Tap one and the map reads '''Signal Source''' and '''Threat Level''' with a
number. A pilot asking for fuel or spare parts is 0 or 1, a shipwreck 0 to 3, and
a fight with Anglers or between pirates and law enforcement 4 or 5. Mission
targets and rating battles are drawn in other colours.

=== Most of them are a choice ===
Events arrive as someone talking to you, and you answer. A stranded pilot asks
for fuel; a pirate tells you to move along; a trader under attack asks for help.
You can always decline, and declining costs nothing.

'''Pirate vs Law is the one with a real decision in it.''' Both sides pitch you
while the fight is already running — ''"I will help the guards"'',
''"I will help the pirates"'', ''"This is not my war"'' — and the side you pick
moves your standing accordingly.

=== What clearing pirate activity pays ===
'''Pirate Activity''' is the event worth going out of your way for. Clear one and
you get '''6 to 9 reputation''', '''1 Special firmware''' and '''+2
[[Combat#Karma|karma]]'''.

The reputation is smarter than it looks. Rather than dumping it on the first
station in the system, the game '''looks for a station whose standing is not
already near the cap''' and pays it there. So clearing pirates works as a way to
lift a station you have neglected, which is exactly the station gating the
[[Ships|ship]] or [[Side quests|side quest]] you want.

=== Helping pays in materials ===
Five event types drop [[Module Mods#Where materials come from|materials]] for
doing nothing more dangerous than stopping:

* '''Give an NPC fuel''' — Fragment of sensors, Chemical processors
* '''Give an NPC spare parts''' — Conductive ceramics, Microresistors
* '''Search a shipwreck''' — Focusing Crystals, Chemical manipulators
* '''Help an NPC against pirates''' — Military alloys, Focusing Crystals
* '''Help an NPC against Anglers''' — Heat diffuser, Conductive polymers

Those eight materials are otherwise a hunt. If you are short one for an
[[Module Mods#What each level costs|upgrade]], answering distress calls is the
cheapest way to find it.
Game Story:
Galaxy Genome tells its story in three places: the '''main story''' that starts with
a new game, the '''side quests''' offered in station bars, and scraps of text such
as bar rumours and the last recordings of lost pilots. None of it is collected in
one place in the game. This page pieces it together, quoting the game's own words.

The first section is safe to read before playing. Everything after it gives the
plot away.

== The setting ==
Humanity has spread out from [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Sol Sol]. The systems around it, the '''Core
Systems''', are long explored: the game says unknown stars begin about 300 light
years out, and the game reminds you that ''“our galaxy is only 0.0003% explored”''.

'''Androids do much of the work.''' They are ''“almost indistinguishable from humans”'',
and on the frontier they are resented for it. A miner at a failing Mining Corp
outpost puts it bluntly: ''“There is almost no work in the Core systems. Androids have taken over every job.”''
A bar rumour adds that the government wants to limit their use.

'''The frontier is poor, the core is rich.''' The same miner: ''“We are here as an underclass. We extract resources for the rich of the Core systems.”''
Drugs move along the trade lanes, pirates hold the lawless systems, and
spectators pay big money to watch pilots wreck each other in the Rating battles.

'''Travel has a history.''' Before the warp drive there were '''warp gates''',
''“the first attempt at long-distance travel”'', abandoned after failed tests when
''“a rival company had successfully test-flighted a warp-drive”''. Their hulks
still hang in space. The warp drive itself came at a cost: when it was being
developed, ''“the scientists of the empire were put into prototype ships. Someone was simply torn to atoms, others disappeared into the depths of space.”''

== The factions ==
Five [[Factions|factions]] own the galaxy's stations. The game gives the three great
powers very different amounts of story.

'''United Empire.''' A military power with a Russian flavour, run in the quests by
General Yuri Gromov from [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=58%20Ophiuchi&station=Gromov%20Platform Gromov Platform]. Gromov sees the
Federation as the aggressor: ''“In recent years, the Trade Federation has been building up forces near our borders. We see constant attempts to seize power in the Senate to push us out of neutral systems. It's time to put an end to this.”''
His answer is ''“Best defense is attack.”''

'''Trade Federation.''' Policed by commissioners with small budgets and large
rivalries, from stations such as [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Wolf%20359&station=Manson%20Orbital Manson Orbital] and
[https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Altair&station=Huton%20Orbital Huton Orbital]. It issues TF-Pass residence papers, tries traitors
before a tribunal, and according to Empire intelligence is building
''“an extremely powerful weapon”''.

'''Interstellar Alliance.''' No Alliance officer speaks in any quest. The weapons
modder Kaito works from one of its stations.

'''Independent''' stations are the frontier: mining outposts, research stations and
hideouts. '''Pirates''' hold three stations and have a cause of their own, shouted
at an Imperial ship: ''“For the independent galaxy!”''

=== Are they at war? ===
'''Not officially.''' Empire and Federation fight a cold war that keeps turning hot:
sabotage, spies and ship losses on both sides, with independent pilots hired to do
the work neither will own. Two Federation commissioners disagree about what to call it:

:''“But we are not at war with them.”'' (Commissioner Pearson)
:''“Not at war? 3 ships in the last week, you hear, 3 ships. They destroyed them. I have no proof, but I know for sure that this is their work.”'' (Commissioner Craig)

In play the conflict stays in the story. In the game's code a faction decides who
owns a station, which [[Ships|ships]] you may buy and which side quests you are
offered, and your standing with it is the sum of your [[Reputation and ranks|reputation]]
at its stations. No rule sends one faction's ships against another's.

== The main story ==
{{spoiler|The main story, from the first job to its ending.}}
=== A job from Marcus ===
You start as a pilot who, the ship's Assistant says, ''“haven't piloted a spaceship for a long time”''.
After the tutorial a smuggler named '''Marcus''' at [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Ross%20720&station=Meridian%20City Meridian City]
offers work, because ''“Everybody needs good pilots now”''. Something is going
wrong: ''“I have a couple of ships flew away n an unknown direction. Damn androids are going crazy.”''

After two honest errands he sends you to [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Alpha%20Centauri&station=Lem%20Hub Lem Hub] with a
cargo that ''“isn't that legal”''. Station security arrests you, and an android
takes over the arrest: '''Investigator Eva-01'''.

=== Eva's case ===
'''Eva''' offers a deal: fly for her and the charges disappear. She needs a human
pilot because ''“machines like me are restricted in their actions towards people”'',
and her case ''“is not official”''. She was built to think like the people she
hunts: ''“I have to think like criminals to catch them.”''

An informant at [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=LHS%202447 LHS 2447] gets out one name before he is shot down:
''“The thing you're looking for is called Galaxy Genome.”'' He also asks Eva
something the game never answers: ''“I wonder if there's something personal here?”''

The trail runs through the archives at Manson Orbital, the head of a security company
in [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=LTT%206774 LTT 6774], and an abandoned laboratory on planet [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Caph Tetra]
in [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Caph Caph], where Galaxy Genome ''“worked on some new generation biological machines”''.
Commissioner '''Pearson''' finds that everyone in its records is dead except one:
'''Dr. Edmond Anger''', hiding at [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=LP%20104-2&station=Mark-01%20Outpost Mark-01 Outpost].

=== The Android ===
Anger admits he led a Galaxy Genome project and that it is connected with the
''“worldwide AI crashes”''. He sends you to the empty-looking system [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Wolf%20851 Wolf 851],
where the abandoned station [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Wolf%20851&station=New%20Horizon New Horizon] hides a figure that calls
itself an android, ''“a close definition at first glance”''.

Its story: Galaxy Genome set out to combine ''“All people's and machines' merits”''
into something ''“suitable for galaxy colonization”'', and ''“I became an embodiment of this new evolution stage.”''
People feared it, so it ran.

In [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Zeta%20Aquilae Zeta Aquilae] it shows what it has built: ''“a program which switches off machine safety protocol”'',
and installs it in Eva. She is freed, and turned. The Android sends her after
'''Jack Trask''', who blocks ''“a project on the equality of people and machines in Congress”''.
In [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Altair Altair] Trask laughs at ''“some piece of iron”'' talking about rights, and dies.

Back at Wolf 359, Pearson argues with her. ''“Freedom doesn't mean going against the will of your creators. Freedom is when you have a choice.”''
Eva: ''“I chose what is valuable for me, and people aren't in this list.”''
Pearson: ''“Is it really your choice? It's just an opinion which was imposed on you.”''

=== Black Sol ===
Shaken, Eva returns to Dr. Anger, who finally tells the truth. The Android is not a
new model. It holds a human donor: '''Ren Sato''', founder of New Horizons Inc.
''“Warp drives, androids – all these things were created under his command.”''
Sato ''“started thinking of himself as God”'' and ''“wanted to trick the death by creating a shell for his consciousness”''.
Rejected, he wanted revenge, and Anger has heard of a warp station he meant to
explode in the Solar system.

You arrive too late. The Android has overloaded the station and the system is destroyed. Eva:
''“You killed millions of people!”'' The Android: ''“If I hadn't done it, nothing would have changed.”''
Its last words, as you destroy it: ''“After all, you are just a machine!”''

'''Sol is gone for good.''' From this point the game renames it '''Black Sol''', its
star becomes a black hole and the system becomes anarchy.

Eva deletes your record, ''“Now you're free”'', and asks to be left at the nearest
station: ''“I even developed a kind of affection towards you. I've never felt something like this before. Maybe it's all because of the system crash.”''
The story ends there, with the achievement '''See You Again'''.

== After the story ==
{{spoiler|Endings of the side quests that continue the main story.}}
Finishing the main story unlocks Commissioner Pearson's quests at Manson Orbital,
starting with [[Side quests##35 Live bait|#35 Live bait]].

'''The machines have lost.''' The use of androids is banned
''“due to recent events”''; Dr. Anger says ''“a real hunt was declared for some models”'',
and Pearson says that without him Eva ''“would have already been sent to the smelter”''.
Eva has been fired. Pearson hid the fact that she became free, so she was never
reflashed. She has taken to reading books, which she could simply download
in an instant.

In [[Side quests##38 Secret lair|#38 Secret lair]] Pearson attacks the pirates' lair in [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=PY%20Vulpeculae PY Vulpeculae] with ships
borrowed from '''Commissioner Craig''' of Altair, and finds Eva among the pirates. She
was undercover all along, and blows up their flagship. Craig arrives, sees
''“a runaway android on the side of the pirates”'', and '''you choose a side'''.
Stand with Eva and Pearson becomes a fugitive; the pair hide in an abandoned research
base in the Pleiades, where, Eva reasons, the Federation will not look. Stand with the
Federation and you kill them both.

== Beyond humanity ==
{{spoiler|The alien races and what the side quests reveal about them.}}
Dr. Landau of [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=93%20Ceti&station=Frontier%20Lab Frontier Lab] says it plainly:
''“Once we considered ourselves the only inhabitants of this galaxy...”'' The side
quests introduce three alien races.

'''Automatons.''' Machine ships in the Pleiades with no sign of life on board, which
Landau names because ''“They act like our search drones, running some kind of automated program...”''
They dig on [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Electra Hellhound] in [https://galaxy-genome.github.io/map/?system=Electra Electra] for fragments of an
alloy that is ''“the 128th element of the periodic table”''. When Landau makes
contact with light signals, the Assistant voices their reply:
''“you... have... ours... give”''. Then General Gromov, who followed him, opens fire,
and afterwards they say only ''“...kill...kill...kill...”''
Officially, hunting them is prohibited. [[Side quests##7 With one eye|#7 With one eye]] starts the chain.

'''Anglers.''' Huge, aggressive creatures that tear cargo ships apart. Dina, who lost
her convoy and her friends to them, calls them bugs; her guess at the name is that
''“The planets are like bait.”'' In [[Side quests##32 Shoulder to shoulder|#32 Shoulder to shoulder]] she leads a fleet of
misfits against them: Dr. Anger's drone ships, Olivia, Kaito and a late Viktor.

'''Zentarks.''' The newest threat, in the LBN 623 nebula, attacking ships while they
are in warp. Their weapon ''“does not fly in a straight line”'' and their ships
appear to teleport. They are living ships: ''“a kind of symbiosis of technology and biological life form. We tried to separate the alien from the ship, but then it's just a pile of metal.”''
Gromov captures one to put in the Rating battles ([[Side quests##44 Pets|#44 Pets]]). It wakes up badly.

=== An ancient war ===
In [[Side quests##30 Bug hunters|#30 Bug hunters]] Landau shows an Automaton plate, ''“a data repository of an ancient civilization”'',
that draws pictures when powered and wetted. It carries three symbols, one for each
race, and a map. Landau reads it: ''“it seems that all three races have already met and by no means for tea drinking. And this map shows their past zones of influence. If this is the Pleiades and this is the Orion cluster, then the center of the battles was near the solar system.”''

Later, an alien stone restarts an abandoned [[Navigation|warp gate]] ([[Side quests##39 Engineering survey|#39 Engineering survey]]).
The game's own repair text asks for a Zentarks Stone.

Ship stats:
What each figure on a ship's stats means in play, how the game works it out, and
which modules move it. The Loadouts planner shows the same
figures; every formula here is the game's own. Figures assume every module at
full integrity and no [[Module Mods]]; a mod scales the figure it names.

== Travel ==
=== Jump ===
How far one warp jump reaches, in light years. The '''Warp Drive''' sets a reach,
and the ship's mass divides it:

* reach = the drive's optimal mass × (1000 × its max fuel ÷ its subclass multiplier) raised to 1 ÷ its class constant
* jump = reach ÷ (mass for jump)

A result above 150 ly is cut to 30 ly. A '''Warp Drive Booster''', when switched
on, then adds its jump range in light years. A bigger or better drive raises
jump; every tonne of module, fuel or cargo lowers it. See [[Navigation]].

=== Supercharged jump ===
Some ships carry a warp supercharge: the next hop may be up to the jump range ×
the ship's multiplier. Leaving a neutron or X-ray star gives ×5 to any ship. The
planner shows the ship's own multiplier; a route uses it for the first hop only.

=== Speed ===
Top speed in light seconds per second. Only the '''Thrusters''' set it:

* speed = the ship's speed × √(thrusters' optimal mass ÷ mass for speed) × 0.0165 × (1 + (grade factor − 1) ÷ 35), never below 0.5

Module mass does not slow the ship; the hull, fuel and cargo do. Engine pips on
the '''Power Distributor''' multiply the result: ×1, ×1.1, ×1.2, ×1.3 for 1 to 4
pips. A heavier hull, full tank or full hold lowers speed.

=== Acceleration ===
Top speed (before engine pips) ÷ 4.5, per second. It moves with speed and
nothing else.

=== Rotation ===
How fast the ship turns: top speed (before engine pips) ÷ 10, which the planner
shows in degrees per second. It moves with speed and nothing else.

=== Tank capacity ===
Fuel the '''Fuel Tank''' holds; a jump burns it. A bigger tank goes further
before refuelling, but a full tank weighs its capacity in tonnes, which counts
against jump and speed.

=== Scoop rate ===
The '''Fuel Scoop''''s rate. It refuels only close enough to a star, and the
closer you are, the more of the rate you get. Without a scoop the figure is
hidden.

=== Scan distance ===
How close a planet must be before flying past it discovers it. The '''Planet
Scanner''' sets it; with none fitted it is 50. Stars are found at any distance.
See [[Exploration]].

=== Sensor range ===
''"The visibility of other spacecrafts is limited by the sensors level on your
ship."'' Ships further than this, in light seconds, are left out of the Objects
list and the nearby ships display. The '''Sensors''' set it: 180 for a 1E up to
345 for an 8A, with grade counting for more than class. With the Sensors off, or
the power plant at 50% integrity or less, the Objects list shows no ships.

== Defence ==
=== Shields ===
How much damage the shields take before they break and the hull starts taking
it. The '''Shields''' module sets a base from the ship's own shield rating:

* base = the ship's shields × (0.53821 × erf(1.0228 × the module's optimal mass ÷ the ship's mass) − 0.0588 × the module's decrease factor + 0.56377)
* shields = base × (1 + the '''Shields Booster''' percentages added together ÷ 100)

A shields module built for a heavier ship gives more, with diminishing returns;
a better grade has a smaller decrease factor. System pips cut damage to the
shields to ×1, ×0.9, ×0.7, ×0.5 for 1 to 4 pips, so 4 pips makes the same shields
last twice as long. See [[Modules#Classes and Grades|Grades]].

=== Recovery speed ===
Shield points restored each second, paid for point by point from the systems
pool of the '''Power Distributor'''. When the pool holds less than a second's
worth, recovery stops. Once broken, shields recover at a separate broken rate
until they are back above half. More system pips refill the pool faster.

=== Hull ===
Damage the hull takes before the ship is destroyed:

* hull = the ship's hull × (1 + the '''Hull''' module's bonus) + every '''Hull Reinforcement''''s points

A heavier hull module or more reinforcement raises it.

=== Hull against damage types ===
The hull points it takes to kill the ship with each damage type, once shields
are down. Damage to the hull is multiplied by the ship's armour, 0.55 + 0.45 ×
25 ÷ its Armour Hardness, then by the type's hull factor and the hull module's
resistance to it (× (1 − resistance)). So a higher Armour Hardness or a hull
module that resists a type raises the figure for that type. See
[[Combat#Damage types|Damage types]].

== Weapons ==
=== Damage per second to shields ===
Damage each second, all weapons firing without a miss, to a target whose
shields are up and which has no resistances. Each weapon deals damage × shots
per second × projectiles × 0.75. The damage type then decides where it lands:

{| class="fandom-table"
! Type !! Shields up: to shields !! Shields up: to hull !! Shields down: to hull
|-
| Thermal (lasers) || 1 || 0 || 0.5
|-
| Kinetic (cannons) || 0.5 || 0 || 1
|-
| Thermal and kinetic (Railgun) || 0.7 || 0.3 || 1
|-
| Plasma || 1 || 0 || 0.65
|-
| Gauss || 1 || 0 || 0.7
|-
| Explosive (missiles, torpedoes, mines) || 0.5 || 0.1 || 1
|}

Each shot also draws weapons pool energy. When the weapons draw is more than the
pool refills, the guns fire only as often as the pool allows, and the figure is
scaled down to match.

=== Damage per second to hull ===
The same, against the hull once the target's shields are down, using the last
column above. A target's armour and resistances cut this further.

=== Fighters ===
What a '''Fighter Hangar''''s wing adds: every fighter alive and firing its own
guns nonstop. The carrier's pips and mods do not change it, so treat it as a
ceiling. '''Total''' is the ship's figure plus the wing's. See
[[Combat#Aircraft carrier|Aircraft carrier]].

=== Mining power ===
The '''Mining Laser''' damage added together. Each hit closes a share of the gap
between a rock's mining progress and done, so progress slows as it nears full.
See [[Mining]].

=== Heat added while firing ===
Degrees per second with every weapon firing: each weapon's heat × the ship's
weapon heat factor. The ship sheds a fixed number of degrees each second while it
is above its base temperature, so if firing adds more, heat climbs. Above 100
degrees the hull takes damage that grows with the temperature, and the game
will not save.

=== Heatsinks ===
Charges in the '''Heatsink Launcher'''. One charge dumps heat for up to 10
seconds, removing more the hotter the ship is.

=== Ammo while firing ===
Credits per second of fire that rearming costs. Only weapons with ammunition
pay; energy weapons do not. Rearming charges each missing round its ammo cost
(at least 1 credit) × the weapon's class, and a shot uses one round per
projectile.

== Cargo ==
=== Cargo capacity ===
Tonnes of cargo the '''Cargo Racks''' hold, added together. Cargo counts against
jump and speed, so the planner shows jump with an empty, half and full hold.

== Power ==
=== Power capacity ===
What the '''Power Plant''' produces. A damaged plant produces less: × (0.8 + 0.2
× integrity).

=== Power priorities ===
'''P1''', '''P1 + P2''' and '''P1 + P2 + P3''' are the power drawn by every module
at that priority or better. When the draw is more than the plant produces, the
game switches off priority 3 modules first, in slot order, then priority 2, then
priority 1, until it fits. It never switches off the plant. The hull, Fuel Tank,
Cargo Racks and Hull Reinforcement draw nothing.

Weapons draw power only while they are deployed, so putting them out is what
usually pushes the draw over. The game suggests choosing what gives way: ''"you
can lower the priority of the warp drive and increase the priority of the weapon.
The warp drive will be disabled if weapon modules are extended, still, there is no
need for the warp drive during the battle."'' You cannot jump with weapons out in
any case ([[Combat#Attack mode|Attack mode]]). Stowing them switches the modules
that were cut back on.

=== Weapons pool refill ===
Energy the '''Power Distributor''' adds to the weapons pool each second: its
weapons rate × weapon pips × 0.25, up to the pool's capacity. The systems and
engine pools work the same way with their own rates and pips.

An empty pool slows its modules down rather than stopping them: ''"In case there
is no energy in the capacitor, the modules will operate with a delay until there
is enough energy to operate in normal mode. For example, guns will fire with a
delay, and it will take longer for the energy shield to recover."'' A weapon waits
for the weapons pool to hold a shot's energy, and shields recharge only while the
systems pool holds enough for the next step.

=== Weapons draw ===
Weapons pool energy used each second with every weapon firing: each shot costs
its power draw ÷ shots per second. A weapon without enough energy in the pool
does not fire.

== Mass ==
=== Mass for jump ===
The hull (the ship's mass × the Hull module's mass factor, kept between 0.8×
and 2× the ship's mass) + every module's mass + fuel + cargo. Jump
divides by it.

=== Mass for speed ===
The hull + fuel + cargo, without modules. Speed divides by it.

== Cost ==
A module costs its price; a Hull module's price is a fraction of the ship's.
Selling a module at full integrity returns its price. Trading in the ship you
fly returns 80% of the ship's price plus 70% of every module outside the main
slots, less the price of the ship's default weapons and extra modules.
